subject: Physics
title: Human Eye: light to sight
description: Explore how light enters the eye, is focused by the lens, and reaches the retina. This enlarged low-poly cutaway is a teaching schematic, not a medical or anatomically scaled model.
learningObjectives: Trace light from the pupil through the lens to the retina.
Explain how the lens focuses light.
Distinguish the retina and optic nerve.

hotspots.label: Retina
hotspots.description: Light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. Photoreceptors convert light into signals that travel through retinal circuits.
hotspots.aiContext: Explain rods and cones, light detection and how signals reach the optic nerve.

hotspots.label: Lens
hotspots.description: The transparent lens changes shape to help focus light on the retina.
hotspots.aiContext: Explain refraction, accommodation, and focusing near or distant objects.

hotspots.label: Pupil
hotspots.description: The opening in the iris through which light enters the eye. The iris changes its size.
hotspots.aiContext: Distinguish the pupil (opening) from the iris (muscular tissue).

hotspots.label: Optic nerve
hotspots.description: Axons of retinal ganglion cells carry visual signals from the eye toward the brain.
hotspots.aiContext: Photoreceptors detect light; the optic nerve transmits signals, not light rays.
